Width for 50 ohm: 0.372 mm.
microstrip 0.372 mm wide on 0.2104 mm, er 4.4 (JLCPCB JLC04161H-7628, outer layer over layer 2 (7628 prepreg)):
  Z0 50 ohm; effective er 3.191 at 2450 MHz
  wavelength on the line 68.5 mm; a quarter wave is 17.13 mm
  Closed-form model (Hammerstad-Jensen), typically within 1–2 %; order impedance control and check the fab's own calculator for the final width.

microstrip 0.0753 mm wide on 0.05 mm, er 4.4:
  Z0 50 ohm; effective er 2.952 at 2450 MHz
  wavelength on the line 71.22 mm; a quarter wave is 17.81 mm
  0.0753 mm is below the 0.1 mm (4 mil) most fabs make reliably; use a thinner dielectric or a wider gap.
  Closed-form model (Hammerstad-Jensen), typically within 1–2 %; order impedance control and check the fab's own calculator for the final width.

Load 20 - j15 ohm at 2450 MHz: return loss 6.59 dB, VSWR 2.76 before matching.
L networks to 50 ohm, listed from the source (radio) side toward the load (antenna):
  1. shunt C 1.59 pF → series L 2.57 nH
     with E24 parts shunt C 1.6 pF → series L 2.7 nH: return loss 25.6 dB, VSWR 1.11
  2. shunt L 2.65 nH → series C 6.84 pF
     with E24 parts shunt L 2.7 nH → series C 6.8 pF: return loss 39.4 dB, VSWR 1.02
Lay the parts out as a pi footprint (shunt-series-shunt, 0402) so either network fits, and fit the final values after measuring the antenna on a VNA: the board, enclosure and hand change its impedance.
Load 50+j0 ohm is already matched to 50 ohm.

  Estimates from a log-distance model; walls, bodies and the enclosure can cost 10–20 dB more. Transmit power and antenna gain must stay within the band's legal limit (EIRP) where the product is sold.

res.port: from the ground plane up to the pin1 pad (1.6 mm probe)

sim.text:
Simulated ANT1 on pcb/rf with openEMS (fast mesh, 200,000 cells, 61 s), fed from the ground plane up to the pin1 pad (1.6 mm probe); swept 1470 MHz to 3430 MHz.
  Best match -18 dB at 2200 MHz; S11 below -10 dB from 2150 MHz to 2260 MHz (110 MHz).
  At 2450 MHz: S11 -3 dB, input impedance 20 + j35 ohm.
  Radiation efficiency 81 %; with the mismatch 50 % of the radio's power is radiated. Peak gain 1.8 dBi toward theta 90°, phi 0° (directivity 2.5 dBi).
  The antenna resonates below the target: shorten its radiating arm by about 10 % and simulate again.
  To match it at 2450 MHz: rf_calc with calc "match", load_re 20, load_im 35, frequency_mhz 2450.
  The model is the antenna's copper, the board substrate, the copper pours and vias; other parts, the enclosure and a hand nearby are not in it and usually pull the resonance down a few percent. Tune the matching network on a VNA before certification.

sim.text:
Simulated ANT1 on pcb/rf with openEMS (fast mesh, 200,000 cells, 61 s), fed from the ground plane up to the pin1 pad (1.6 mm probe); swept 1470 MHz to 3430 MHz.
  Best match only -1.6 dB, at 1430 MHz: S11 never reaches -10 dB in the sweep.
  At 2450 MHz: S11 -0.6 dB, input impedance 169 + j477 ohm.
  Radiation efficiency 81 %; with the mismatch 50 % of the radio's power is radiated. Peak gain 1.8 dBi toward theta 90°, phi 0° (directivity 2.5 dBi).
  Warning: 100 % of the antenna's trace has ground copper under it or within 2 mm beside it, which turns it into a transmission line rather than an antenna (low, lossy resonance, poor match). Keep every layer's pour out from under and around the radiating arm: put a <keepout> over the antenna area, or place the antenna at a board edge beyond the ground plane, then rebuild and simulate again.
  To match it at 2450 MHz: rf_calc with calc "match", load_re 169, load_im 477, frequency_mhz 2450.
  The model is the antenna's copper, the board substrate, the copper pours and vias; other parts, the enclosure and a hand nearby are not in it and usually pull the resonance down a few percent. Tune the matching network on a VNA before certification.
